question.latex:
![Diagrams of two magnetic wire configurations]$https://cracku.in/media/uploads/image_4yvtbH5.png$
Two identical long current carrying wires are bent into the shapes shown in figures. Shape $I$ consists of a U-turn featuring a semicircle where the current enters, loops, and leaves parallel. Shape $II$ consists of a semi-infinite wire leading into a semicircle, ending such that the exiting semi-infinite wire aligns radially outward giving zero contribution at center. If the magnitude of magnetic fields at the centres P and Q of a semicircular arc are $B_1$ and $B_2$ respectively, then the ratio $B_1 / B_2$ is _______.
question.unicode:
![Diagrams of two magnetic wire configurations]https://cracku.in/media/uploads/image_4yvtbH5.png
Two identical long current carrying wires are bent into the shapes shown in figures. Shape I consists of a U-turn featuring a semicircle where the current enters, loops, and leaves parallel. Shape II consists of a semi-infinite wire leading into a semicircle, ending such that the exiting semi-infinite wire aligns radially outward giving zero contribution at center. If the magnitude of magnetic fields at the centres P and Q of a semicircular arc are B_1 and B_2 respectively, then the ratio B_1 / B_2 is _______.
question.plainText: ![Diagrams of two magnetic wire configurations]https://cracku.in/media/uploads/image_4yvtbH5.png Two identical long current carrying wires are bent into the shapes shown in figures. Shape I consists of a U-turn featuring a semicircle where the current enters, loops, and leaves parallel. Shape II consists of a semi-infinite wire leading into a semicircle, ending such that the exiting semi-infinite wire aligns radially outward giving zero contribution at center. If the magnitude of magnetic fields at the centres P and Q of a semicircular arc are B_1 and B_2 respectively, then the ratio B_1 / B_2 is _______.

explanation.latex:
Let's find the magnetic field at the center of the semicircles for both configurations.
For Configuration (I) (the hair-pin loop), the magnetic field at center P has three components:
1. Top semi-infinite straight wire: $B = \frac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi R}$ pointing downwards ($\otimes$).
2. Semicircular arc: $B = \frac{\mu_0 I}{4 R} = \frac{\pi\mu_0 I}{4\pi R}$ pointing downwards ($\otimes$).
3. Bottom semi-infinite straight wire (flowing back): $B = \frac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi R}$ pointing downwards ($\otimes$).
Total $B_1 = \frac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi R} (1 + \pi + 1) = \frac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi R}(2 + \pi)$.

For Configuration (II), the magnetic field at center Q is the sum of:
1. One top semi-infinite straight wire at distance R: $B = \frac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi R}$ pointing downwards ($\otimes$).
2. Semicircular arc: $B = \frac{\mu_0 I}{4 R} = \frac{\pi\mu_0 I}{4\pi R}$ pointing downwards ($\otimes$).
3. The exiting wire is placed such that its line passes through Q, contributing $0$ field.
Total $B_2 = \frac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi R} (1 + \pi + 0) = \frac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi R}(1 + \pi)$.

The ratio is $\frac{B_1}{B_2} = \frac{2 + \pi}{1 + \pi}$.
explanation.unicode:
Let's find the magnetic field at the center of the semicircles for both configurations.
For Configuration (I) (the hair-pin loop), the magnetic field at center P has three components:
1. Top semi-infinite straight wire: B = (mu_0 I/4π R) pointing downwards (otimes).
2. Semicircular arc: B = (mu_0 I/4 R) = (πmu_0 I/4π R) pointing downwards (otimes).
3. Bottom semi-infinite straight wire (flowing back): B = (mu_0 I/4π R) pointing downwards (otimes).
Total B_1 = (mu_0 I/4π R) (1 + π + 1) = (mu_0 I/4π R)(2 + π).

For Configuration (II), the magnetic field at center Q is the sum of:
1. One top semi-infinite straight wire at distance R: B = (mu_0 I/4π R) pointing downwards (otimes).
2. Semicircular arc: B = (mu_0 I/4 R) = (πmu_0 I/4π R) pointing downwards (otimes).
3. The exiting wire is placed such that its line passes through Q, contributing 0 field.
Total B_2 = (mu_0 I/4π R) (1 + π + 0) = (mu_0 I/4π R)(1 + π).

The ratio is (B_1/B_2) = (2 + π/1 + π).

question.latex: A particle having charge $10^{-9}\text{ C}$ moving in $x$-$y$ plane in fields of $0.4\hat{j}\text{ N/C}$ and $4 \times 10^{-3}\hat{k}\text{ T}$ experiences a force of $$4\hat{i} + 2\hat{j}$ \times 10^{-10}\text{ N}$. The velocity of the particle at that instant is _______ m/s.
question.unicode: A particle having charge 10^{-9}text{ C} moving in x-y plane in fields of 0.4hat{j}text{ N/C} and 4 × 10^{-3}hat{k}text{ T} experiences a force of 4hat{i} + 2hat{j} × 10^{-10}text{ N}. The velocity of the particle at that instant is _______ m/s.
question.plainText: A particle having charge 10^{-9}text{ C} moving in x-y plane in fields of 0.4hat{j}text{ N/C} and 4 times 10^{-3}hat{k}text{ T} experiences a force of 4hat{i} + 2hat{j} times 10^{-10}text{ N}. The velocity of the particle at that instant is _______ m/s.

explanation.latex:
Let velocity $\vec{v} = v_x \hat{i} + v_y \hat{j}$. Lorentz force $\vec{F} = q(\vec{E} + \vec{v} \times \vec{B})$.
$\vec{v} \times \vec{B} = (v_x \hat{i} + v_y \hat{j}) \times (4 \times 10^{-3} \hat{k}) = 4 \times 10^{-3} v_x (-\hat{j}) + 4 \times 10^{-3} v_y (\hat{i})$.
The net force is $\vec{F} = 10^{-9} \left[ (4 \times 10^{-3} v_y)\hat{i} + (0.4 - 4 \times 10^{-3} v_x)\hat{j} \right]$.
Given $\vec{F} = 4 \times 10^{-10} \hat{i} + 2 \times 10^{-10} \hat{j}$. Comparing components:
x-component: $10^{-9} (4 \times 10^{-3} v_y) = 4 \times 10^{-10} \implies 4v_y = 400 \implies v_y = 100\text{ m/s}$.
y-component: $10^{-9} (0.4 - 4 \times 10^{-3} v_x) = 2 \times 10^{-10} \implies 0.4 - 4 \times 10^{-3} v_x = 0.2 \implies 4 \times 10^{-3} v_x = 0.2 \implies v_x = \frac{0.2}{0.004} = 50\text{ m/s}$.
Therefore, $\vec{v} = 50\hat{i} + 100\hat{j}\text{ m/s}$.

The net force is vec{F} = 10^{-9} left[ (4 × 10^{-3} v_y)hat{i} + (0.4 - 4 × 10^{-3} v_x)hat{j} right].
Given vec{F} = 4 × 10^{-10} hat{i} + 2 × 10^{-10} hat{j}. Comparing components:
x-component: 10^{-9} (4 × 10^{-3} v_y) = 4 × 10^{-10} implies 4v_y = 400 implies v_y = 100text{ m/s}.

Therefore, vec{v} = 50hat{i} + 100hat{j}text{ m/s}.

question.latex: $1\text{ }\mu\text{C}$ charge moving with velocity $\vec{v} = $\hat{i} - 2\hat{j} + 3\hat{k}$\text{ m/s}$ in the region of magnetic field $\vec{B} = $2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} - 5\hat{k}$\text{ T}$. The magnitude of force acting on it is $\sqrt{\alpha} \times 10^{-6}\text{ N}$. The value of $\alpha$ is _______.
question.unicode: 1text{ }mutext{C} charge moving with velocity vec{v} = hat{i} - 2hat{j} + 3hat{k}text{ m/s} in the region of magnetic field vec{B} = 2hat{i} + 3hat{j} - 5hat{k}text{ T}. The magnitude of force acting on it is √(α) × 10^{-6}text{ N}. The value of α is _______.
question.plainText: 1text{ }mutext{C} charge moving with velocity vec{v} = hat{i} - 2hat{j} + 3hat{k}text{ m/s} in the region of magnetic field vec{B} = 2hat{i} + 3hat{j} - 5hat{k}text{ T}. The magnitude of force acting on it is sqrt(alpha) times 10^{-6}text{ N}. The value of alpha is _______.

explanation.latex:
The Lorentz magnetic force on a moving charge is $\vec{F} = q(\vec{v} \times \vec{B})$.
Let's calculate the cross product $\vec{v} \times \vec{B}$:
$\vec{v} \times \vec{B} = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 1 & -2 & 3 \\ 2 & 3 & -5 \end{vmatrix}$
$= \hat{i}((-2)(-5) - (3)(3)) - \hat{j}((1)(-5) - (3)(2)) + \hat{k}((1)(3) - (-2)(2))$
$= \hat{i}(10 - 9) - \hat{j}(-5 - 6) + \hat{k}(3 + 4)$
$= 1\hat{i} - (-11)\hat{j} + 7\hat{k} = \hat{i} + 11\hat{j} + 7\hat{k}$
The magnitude is $|\vec{v} \times \vec{B}| = \sqrt{1^2 + 11^2 + 7^2} = \sqrt{1 + 121 + 49} = \sqrt{171}$.
The magnitude of the force is $|\vec{F}| = q|\vec{v} \times \vec{B}| = (1 \times 10^{-6}) \sqrt{171}\text{ N}$.
Rewriting this as $\sqrt{171} \times 10^{-6}\text{ N}$, we can directly observe that $\alpha = 171$.

= 1hat{i} - (-11)hat{j} + 7hat{k} = hat{i} + 11hat{j} + 7hat{k}
The magnitude is |vec{v} × vec{B}| = √(1² + 11² + 7²) = √(1 + 121 + 49) = √(171).
The magnitude of the force is |vec{F}| = q|vec{v} × vec{B}| = (1 × 10^{-6}) √(171)text{ N}.
Rewriting this as √(171) × 10^{-6}text{ N}, we can directly observe that α = 171.
